initial_candidates.title: container.empty() not explicitly clearing when refreshes/streaming data is needed via st.rerun()
initial_candidates.text:
### Additional Information

_No response_

This issue reports that calling `container.empty()` followed by `st.rerun()` does not immediately clear the container's contents on the frontend. Instead, the old elements linger as "stale" (greyed-out) elements until the next script run fully completes. The root cause is in how Streamlit's render tree works: when a new script run begins, keyed containers inherit their children from the previous run (see `addBlock` in `AppRoot.ts`). These inherited children are marked as stale (via `isElementStale` in `Block/utils.ts`) and rendered with reduced opacity, but they are only actually removed from the tree when `clearStaleNodes` is called at the **end** of the script run. In the reporter's case, a `time.sleep(2)` polling loop means stale elements remain visible for the full duration of each run, causing a "pulsing" effect. The `container.empty()` call from the previous run has no lasting effect since the container is re-created with inherited children in the new run.

In this example, we access `st.session_state.name` both before and after the buttons which modify it. When a button ("**Jane**" or "**John**") is clicked, the script reruns. This issue reports that calling `container.empty()` followed by `st.rerun()` does not immediately clear the container's contents on the frontend. Instead, the old elements linger as "stale" (greyed-out) elements until the next script run fully completes. The root cause is in how Streamlit's render tree works: when a new script run begins, keyed containers inherit their children from the previous run (see `addBlock` in `AppRoot.ts`). These inherited children are marked as stale (via `isElementStale` in `Block/utils.ts`) and rendered with reduced opacity, but they are only actually removed from the tree when `clearStaleNodes` is called at the **end** of the script run. In the reporter's case, a `time.sleep(2)` polling loop means stale elements remain visible for the full duration of each run, causing a "pulsing" effect. The `container.empty()` call from the previous run has no lasting effect since the container is re-created with inherited children in the new run.","title":"container.empty() not explicitly clearing when refreshes/streaming data is needed via st.rerun()","url":"https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14280","version_relation":"unknown"},{"id":"issue:11266:v2:b0b00ad71c9d0511","kind":"issue","lines":[62,103],"product_version":null,"revision":"2025-05-07T14:09:05Z","section":"Additional Information","source_authority":"reported_observation","source_id":"issue:11266","temporal_status":"not_historical","text":"### Additional Information
